question: What will the US core PCE year-over-year inflation rate for September 2026 be, released October 29, 2026?

calls.reasoning: August core PCE was 3.01% unrounded (CNBC). Post-CPI/PPI translations of September core m/m range 0.29-0.35% (CNBC survey of 7, median ~0.32%), giving ~3.10% y/y after the ~0.23% September-2025 base effect. Employ America says 3.09%, TD 3.1%, Timiraos 3.1%, Cleveland Fed nowcast 3.05%. Central mass sits inside the 3.05-3.15 rounding band, so 3.1 is modal (~70%). Downside risk to 3.0 comes from a low m/m or downward prior-month revisions (EA sees August revised down ~2bp); upside to 3.2 needs m/m >= ~0.37%. Polymarket on the identical contract (~$21k volume): 3.1 ~54%, 3.0 ~19%, 3.2 ~13% — wider than my distribution, same mode. Manifold >=0.3% m/m ~71%, Polymarket MoM 0.3% ~67%, both consistent.
calls.dossier:
- BEA Aug 2026 release (Sep 30, 2026): core PCE +0.2% m/m, 3.0% y/y; headline 3.4% y/y. The annual update rewrote data back to Jan 2021 and lowered every 2026 month; July was revised from 3.3% to 3.0% (techtimes, portfolio-terminal).
- Unrounded August core y/y is 3.01% (CNBC, Oct 15, 2026).
- CNBC survey of 7 sell-side forecasts after the September PPI (Oct 15): September core PCE m/m averages 0.32%, range 0.29% (Oxford) to 0.35% (Barclays); the article says this implies 3.1% y/y.
- Employ America Core-Cast after PPI: +0.34% m/m, 3.09% y/y (down from 3.12%); expects August m/m revised down ~2bp to 0.23% (airfares, hospitals).
- TD Securities (FXStreet, Oct 15): core 0.32% m/m (from 0.36% after CPI), core y/y 3.1%, headline 3.6%.
- Morgan Stanley 0.34% m/m; Pantheon 0.36%; Oxford 0.29% (Newsquawk via search summary).
- Cleveland Fed nowcast (updated 10/16): September core PCE 0.28% m/m, 3.05% y/y.
- Nick Timiraos (X): projection ~0.34% m/m gives 3.1% y/y and 3-month annualized 2.9%.
- September PPI rose 1.3% m/m vs 0.6% expected, driven by airfares. September CPI was hot (headline 3.7% y/y).
- Implied September 2025 base m/m is ~0.22-0.23% (from 3.01 + 0.32 = ~3.10).
- Rounding bands: 3.0 needs unrounded <3.05; 3.1 is 3.05-3.15; 3.2 is >=3.15, which needs roughly m/m >=0.37% with no revisions.
- Resolves off BEA 'Change From Month One Year Ago' core PCE table, first print, one decimal; not CPI and not later revisions.
- Event window: single release Oct 29, 2026 8:30 ET; as of Oct 19, all inputs (CPI, PPI) are already out, and only revisions and translation error remain.
- Status quo: the prior three prints were 3.0%.
- Searched for but not found: an exact BEA-revised September 2025 m/m figure; a Bloomberg consensus number.
calls.reference_class: Core PCE y/y prints vs post-CPI/PPI sell-side translations, which historically miss m/m by about +/-0.03-0.05pp

calls.reasoning: August core PCE was 3.01% YoY before rounding (+0.25% m/m), with a ~2bp downward revision expected, so the September YoY ≈ 2.99 + (Sept m/m - ~0.24). Post-CPI/PPI nowcasts: Employ America, Morgan Stanley and Timiraos 0.34% (→3.09%), TD 0.32%, Oxford 0.29% (→3.0%). Rounding to 3.1 needs m/m ~0.30-0.39; centred at 0.33 with SD ~0.05: ~27% falls below the 0.30 line, ~8% reaches 0.40. Polymarket's matching but thin (~$21k) multi-outcome book: 3.1 ~54%, 3.0 ~19%, 3.2 ~13%, 2.9 ~10%. My split: 3.1 ~60%, 3.0 ~25%, 3.2 ~10%. No escape mass beyond the bounds.
calls.dossier:
- BEA core PCE YoY published: May 2026 3.2, Jun 3.0, Jul 3.0, Aug 3.0 (BEA page, release 2026-09-30).
- Aug 2026 core PCE before rounding: +0.25% m/m, 3.01% YoY (Employ America August post-PCE note).
- Employ America post-PPI (mid-Oct 2026): expects Aug m/m revised down ~2bp to ~0.23 because of airfare/hospital revisions; September nowcast +0.34% m/m, 3.09% YoY. Implied Sept 2025 base m/m ≈ 0.24 (inferred, not directly confirmed).
- Arithmetic: Sept YoY ≈ 2.99 + (Sept m/m - 0.24). Rounds to 3.0 if m/m < ~0.30, to 3.1 if ~0.30-0.39, to 3.2 if ≥ ~0.40.
- WSJ's Timiraos (X, ~Oct 15): CPI+PPI translate to ~0.34% m/m; 12-month rate 3.1%, 3-month annualized rate 2.9%.
- Morgan Stanley: Sept core PCE 0.34% m/m, headline 0.51% (via search snippet). TD Securities: lowered to 0.32% m/m after soft PPI components (snippet). Oxford Economics: 0.29% m/m, 3.0% YoY (snippet).
- Drivers: September CPI core beat (0.3% vs 0.2% consensus); PPI airfares hot, other PCE-relevant PPI inputs benign.
- Upside to the base: headline CPI 3.7% YoY; Fed expected to hold in Oct and hike in Dec. Downside: soft PPI health/portfolio components; prior months can be revised in the Oct 29 release.
- Status quo: three straight 3.0 prints.
- Resolves off the BEA core PCE page's 'Change From Month One Year Ago' figure for September 2026 as first published, not Trading Economics or the market consensus.
- Event window: release 2026-10-29 08:30 EDT; as of 2026-10-19 the data month is complete, so only translation uncertainty remains.
- Searched without success: official Sept 2025 base m/m; Goldman, JPM and Citi nowcasts.

Consensus Sep m/m ~0.32 (range 0.28-0.36) gives ~3.07-3.09 unrounded, so 3.1 is modal (~60%). 3.0 needs m/m below ~0.29 or downward revisions (~25%); 3.2 needs ~0.39+ (~12%). calls.reconciliation: Main factual dispute: the Sep-2025 base m/m (Run 3 ~0.20 from recall, Runs 1-2 ~0.23-0.24). Settled toward ~0.24 by back-solving the published nowcast pairs (Cleveland 0.28->3.05; Employ America 0.34->3.09 net of a -2bp Aug revision), so Run 3's arithmetic runs ~3bp hot. Whether Aug gets revised down 2bp cannot be checked until release, so it stays as uncertainty. Judgment: 3.0 is a real tail because two nowcasts (Oxford, Cleveland) sit at the rounding line; Polymarket's 10% on 2.9 looks unsupported. Kept Run 2's somewhat lower center; no escape mass beyond the bounds.
